No. Drafts are saved for a person to review and send. This keeps control with your team and avoids a wrong answer reaching a customer.
Does it work with Gmail, Outlook or Zendesk?
Yes, all three, along with Help Scout, Freshdesk and Gorgias. Tell us what you use and we confirm the method before we start.
How will drafts match my voice?

desc:
AI email reply drafts for support teams save hours of typing without taking control away from your people. Ecom Swift LLC sets up drafting in your own inbox, so every new customer email arrives with a suggested reply written in your tone, ready for a person to check and send.

## What are AI email reply drafts for support teams?

AI email reply drafts are suggested answers that appear in your support inbox as saved drafts, next to the customer message they respond to. The tool reads the incoming email, matches it to a question type you have defined, and writes a reply using your policies and your past wording. A team member reads the draft, changes anything that needs changing and presses send. The tool never sends on its own.

## Why drafting beats writing every reply from scratch

Most support inboxes are full of the same dozen questions: where an order is, how a return works, whether an item is in stock, how to change an address. Agents answer each one by searching old threads, copying a paragraph and fixing the details. That is slow, and the tone drifts from one person to the next, and from morning to evening.

A draft removes the blank page. The agent starts with a complete, correct-sounding answer and spends the time on judgment instead of typing. New staff also learn your voice faster, because every draft shows them how you write.

## How drafts change speed and quality

Reply speed shapes how customers feel about a business. A customer who waits a day for a simple answer often writes a second time, which doubles the work. Drafts shorten the time between opening an email and sending a good answer, so the queue shrinks and fewer follow-ups arrive.

Quality improves because the draft draws on one agreed source of truth. If your refund wording is written once, every draft uses it, so two agents do not give two different answers. Because a human still approves each message, odd or sensitive cases get the care they need.

## What a strong drafting setup includes

- A connection to your shared support inbox that saves drafts instead of sending.
- A list of question types, each with the facts a correct answer must contain.
- Your tone, learned from real past replies you approve as examples.
- Greeting, sign-off and signature rules that match each team member or brand.
- Customer name and order number filled in where the email contains them.
- Policy lines for returns, shipping and warranty that drafts must follow.
- A marker on drafts that need extra care, so agents read them slowly.
- A way to flag emails the tool should not draft at all.
- A review of how often agents edit drafts, so the setup keeps improving.

## What we do

We start by reading a sample of your recent support emails and sorting them into question types. We write the rules for each type, connect the draft tool to your inbox with limited access, and test it on past emails so you can compare the drafts with what your team actually sent.

The Basic package covers your most frequent questions in one inbox. The Standard package widens the coverage, fills in names and order details, and tests on a larger batch of past emails. The Premium package adds policy checks before a draft is saved, a regular sheet showing what your team edited, and a handover guide with a call. Each package ends with drafts running in your live inbox and your team knowing how to adjust them.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share replies you are proud of, not only the average ones.
- Keep one person responsible for approving changes to the rules.
- Read every draft before sending, especially in the first weeks.
- Update the rules whenever a policy changes.

**Avoid:**
- Letting drafts go out without a person reading them.
- Drafting for angry, legal or safety related emails.
- Mixing old and new policy wording in the examples.
- Judging the setup on one bad draft instead of the pattern of edits.
- Adding question types faster than your team can review them.

## Who this is for

A small online store owner who answers every email personally and wants evenings back. A support lead with two or three agents who sound different from one another. A growing brand using Gmail, Outlook or a help desk that needs faster first replies during sales peaks.

## What we need from you

Send access to the inbox as a collaborator, delegate or team user, never a password. Share ten to twenty past replies you like, your return and shipping policies, and any phrases you never want used. We confirm the question types with you before building, then keep you updated until drafts appear in your inbox.
